overview.headline: How cosine and other functions link angle values to side ratios

keyPoints.point: Students learn a function means the value of one variable depends uniquely on another variable.
keyPoints.quote: the value of one variable in a problem depends uniquely on the value of another variable in the problem.

keyPoints.point: Students learn exponential function relates a variable to how many times another variable is used as a multiplier.
keyPoints.quote: The exponential function relates a variable to the number of times another variable is used as a multiplier

keyPoints.point: Students learn trigonometric functions are defined by ratio of sides that depends only on angle, not single side length.
keyPoints.quote: The trigonometric functions are defined in terms of the ratio of the length of the sides of a right triangle

keyPoints.point: Students learn scaling a right triangle by 2 or 3 keeps cosine as x divided by y after simplifying.
keyPoints.quote: For the red triangle, the cosine of “b” is equal to 2x divided by 2y.

keyTerms.gloss: mathematical concept where one variable depends uniquely on another variable
keyTerms.quote: An important mathematical concept is the idea of function

keyTerms.gloss: trigonometric ratio of adjacent side to hypotenuse for a given angle in a right triangle
keyTerms.quote: For the black triangle, the cosine of “b” is equal to x divided by y.

keyTerms.gloss: longest side of a right triangle opposite the right angle, labeled h in the example
keyTerms.quote: The black triangle is the smallest triangle and has a hypotenuse “h” of length “y” and an adjacent side “a” equal to “x”.

keyTerms.gloss: trigonometric function that relates sides and angles of a triangle
keyTerms.quote: The trigonometric functions sine, cosine, and tangent relate the various sides and angles of a triangle.
